name: AMERICAN INTEGRITY INSURANCE GROUP

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest counter is that this pass should have upgraded to cheap and did not. The 2026-09-04 verdict was capped at no_edge for one stated reason — the size of the retained loss in a landfall year was unknown — and that reason is now gone. A single event costs $35 million, which is 9.5% of equity and less than one quarter's pre-tax income. The worst season the programme is modelled against costs $75 million, roughly 20% of equity and about three quarters of one year's earnings: a bad year, not an impairment. The reinsurance was bought MORE cheaply with a LOWER aggregate retention despite 19% exposure growth, which is the opposite of a carrier reaching for risk. And I initially read 1H adjusted net income of $54.7 million against $69.4 million as the margin compression the last pass predicted — that reading was wrong and I corrected it: 1H 2025 carried income tax expense of only $1.4 million because the company was an LLC until its May 2025 IPO, and on a pre-tax basis income ROSE 10% ($73.7M against $67.0M) with second-quarter pre-tax income up 93%. The combined ratio 'deterioration' to 68.5% is likewise the quota-share reduction moving ceding commission income out of the expense line, which the deck explains. At a 16% sustainable ROTCE on the correct $18.86 book the fair value is about $34.29, or +35%.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Two things would settle it in the bull's favour: the 2027 June 1 renewal pricing down again on a second consecutive quiet season, and Florida primary rate filings holding rather than following. Against it: any Q3 or Q4 2026 disclosure of retained catastrophe losses, or a 2027 filing showing average premium per policy falling more than low single digits.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The bounded tail is visible and verified. What is ALSO visible, and is what stops me, is that the entire favourable resolution is already in the tape: the shares are +49.5% over 63 days and +37.3% over twelve months into the quietest Atlantic hurricane season on record. Buying a single-state Florida catastrophe writer in mid-September after the risk has largely resolved is buying after the news, and the next two quiet seasons push reinsurance and then primary rates lower — the company's own competitive-environment slide already shows average premium per policy down year over year while it grows policies in force 16%.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The cost of equity, and it is decisive. The engine's 9.7% comes from a sector-median beta of 0.87 substituted because AII's own regression has an R-squared of 0.010 — and the Financials median is built from banks and diversified financials. A single-state Florida homeowners insurer whose earnings distribution is bimodal around landfall does not have a 0.87 beta. At the engine's 9.7% cost of equity my 16% ROTCE justifies 1.82x book and the name is +35%. At a defensible 12-13% for this risk profile the justified multiple is 1.27-1.39 and the gap is roughly zero to -6%. The schema has no field to override cost of equity, so the sign of this verdict is set by an input I cannot correct and did not choose. Also still unresolved from the last pass: reserve adequacy on pre-reform accident years, with only fifteen months of public reporting, and the fact that this company has still never been observed through a catastrophe as a public entity — and on current form 2026 will not provide that observation either.

what_changed: I fetched the document the last devil's-advocate pass nominated and could not obtain, and it answers the question that capped that verdict. The 2026-09-08 investor deck (8-K Item 7.01, EX-99.1) discloses the finalised 2026/2027 catastrophe excess-of-loss programme in full: FIRST EVENT RETENTION OF $35.0 MILLION ($10M at the insurance entity, $25M at the captive), unchanged from last year despite 19% exposure growth; second event retention $20 million; third and fourth event retentions $10 million each; and AGGREGATE RETENTION IN A FOUR-EVENT SEASON REDUCED FROM $95 MILLION TO $75 MILLION. The first-event tower including retentions is $2.27 billion, a 1-in-130 year probable maximum loss, total third-party coverage for all occurrences is $3.0 billion (up $409 million, 15.8%), the programme cost $430-440 million, and it was placed at a risk-adjusted rate reduction at the high end of 15-20%. The tower is modelled to contain a repeat of the four-event 2004 Florida storm season. Separately: 1H 2026 gross premiums written $546.6M (+10%), net premiums earned $186.9M (+42%, on the quota share cut from 40% to 25%), pre-tax income $73.7M against $67.0M, policies in force +16% and voluntary +22%, policy retention up from 75.1% to 84.4%, voluntary new business gross written premium $35.1M to $87.7M. And the season itself: as of 11 September 2026 the Atlantic has produced five named storms and ZERO hurricanes — a record for the latest first hurricane — with accumulated cyclone energy of 4.4 against a normal 58.2, and no tropical development expected in the following seven days.
consensus_case: At $25.41 against a corrected tangible book of $18.86, American Integrity trades at 1.35x book while reporting a 40% adjusted return on equity in the second quarter and 31% for the half. The market is therefore implying a sustainable return of roughly 12% — that returns fall by about two-thirds. The bear case for that is coherent: Florida primary rates are flattening while reinsurance costs fall faster, the company's own deck concedes 'reinsurance rates have been declining well in excess of primary rates', average gross written premium per policy already slipped from $2,178 to $2,156 year over year, and the 63.4% combined ratio is the best this business will ever look — a no-catastrophe quarter in a reformed market with capital flooding back in. A single-state Florida homeowners insurer at the statistical peak of hurricane season, up 49.5% in 63 days, priced at only 1.35x book is the market declining to capitalise a peak-cycle return.
base_case_rationale: Not applicable — book method. My sustainable ROTCE is 16%, unchanged from the 2026-09-04 pass. The new information bounds the downside rather than raising the mean: knowing that a landfall costs $35 million and the worst modelled season costs $75 million tells me the distribution has a floor, not that the average is higher. Against that, 2026 is on track to be the quietest Atlantic season on record, which is the single best possible year for this business and is exactly the year being annualised into a 40% adjusted ROE. Through a cycle that includes landfall years, reserve development on pre-reform accident years, and primary rates following reinsurance costs down, 16% is a return well above the cost of equity and well below what is being printed today.
key_risks: The verdict's sign is set by a 9.7% cost of equity derived from a sector-median beta (own R-squared 0.010) on a single-state Florida catastrophe writer; at 12-13% the gap disappears entirely
The engine's 28.9% 'sustainable' ROTCE is a SINGLE observation — the extract holds exactly one year of net income and one of equity
Shares +49.5% over 63 days into the quietest Atlantic season on record; the favourable resolution is largely priced
Primary rates are already flattening while reinsurance falls faster — the company's own deck concedes it and average premium per policy is down year over year
Reserve development on pre-SB-2A accident years, with fifteen months of public reporting
A storm larger than the 1-in-130 year tower attachment leaves loss above $2.27 billion with the company
Record voluntary new business (+150% premium) written into a softening primary rate environment is how Florida carriers have historically bought trouble
watch_for: Any named storm making Florida landfall before 30 November 2026 and the retained loss disclosed against the $35 million first-event retention
Q3 2026 combined ratio — the first full season quarter, and the test of whether 63.4% was expense discipline or weather
Florida OIR primary rate filings: reinsurance falling is good for AII only until primary rates follow
The 2027 June 1 catastrophe excess-of-loss renewal — a second consecutive risk-adjusted decrease confirms capital inflow and confirms the rate-compression bear case at the same time
Average gross written premium per policy: $2,156 at Q2 2026 against $2,178 a year earlier
